history.reason: The v0.1 A1 profile implicitly assumed the ability to interpret recursively defined rules. The literature re-audit judged that capability too computationally strong to hide inside a generic mathematical prior. v0.2 separates elementary mathematical concepts from an exact rule calculus R.

atoms.statement: The receiver is given two distinguished logical symbols with an agreed mapping to binary 0 and 1.
Received logical symbols form a finite sequence with an agreed first-to-last order.
The exact start, end, and bit length of the measured frame are available to the receiver.
The measured frame is delivered without residual bit errors; physical noise handling is below this model boundary.
The parties share the concept of non-negative integers, zero, successor, equality, ordering, addition, and subtraction where defined.
The parties share finite sequences, sequence length, concatenation, and positional indexing as mathematical concepts.

A parameter R names one exact formal rule calculus, including its finite syntax, binding/substitution conventions if any, operational interpretation, recursion convention, and binary serialization/framing.
A parameter U names one exact fixed universal binary abstract machine whose operational semantics are already shared.
For the same U, the program/data boundary and self-delimiting binary input convention are already shared exactly.
A parameter H names a concrete terrestrial execution platform, language/runtime, ABI, or equivalent host environment.

profiles.name: digital transport prior
explicitly_not_assumed: NEX term grammar or primitive IDs
any terrestrial processor, ABI, OS, language, or runtime

profiles.name: elementary discrete-mathematics prior
explicitly_not_assumed: a syntax for executable or recursive rule descriptions
Elias gamma or any particular integer code
NEX term grammar or primitive IDs
a universal machine or instruction set

profiles.name: exact formal-rule-calculus prior

parameter.name: R
parameter.constraint: R must be versioned and must fix exact formal syntax, semantics, recursion/binding rules, and binary serialization before any B | A1(R) claim is accepted.

explicitly_not_assumed: NEX term grammar or primitive IDs unless explicitly encoded in R
a universal machine unless R itself defines one

profiles.name: fixed universal-machine prior

parameter.name: U
parameter.constraint: U must have a versioned exact binary operational semantics and exact program/data framing before any B | A2(U) measurement is accepted.

explicitly_not_assumed: NEX term grammar or primitive IDs
a terrestrial host unless U itself explicitly is one, in which case the claim is not receiver-neutral

parameter.name: H
parameter.constraint: H must identify an exact host language/runtime/platform version.

accounting.exact_message_form: C | A = |M_A|, where M_A is the exact transmitted object under declared profile A
accounting.rule: Every transmitted bit is counted exactly once. If a bit cannot be defensibly partitioned between specification and executable bootstrap roles, it belongs to one joint SB segment rather than both S and B.
accounting.program_payload: For a fixed NEX wire contract, the canonical program bit length is exact. It is a conditional description length under that established contract, not an unconditional machine-free information quantity.
